The effects fall into two groups that do not always appear together. In blood, red cells are produced larger than usual and haemoglobin can fall. In the nervous system, the insulating sheath around nerves is affected, which can produce tingling, numbness, unsteadiness and, over longer periods, effects on memory and mood.
